chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Sa'id ibn Janah, who said: Abu Mas'ud narrated to me from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Whoever says four times when it is morning, 'Al-hamdu lillahi rabb al-'alamin' (Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds), has fulfilled the gratitude of his day; and whoever says it when it is evening, has fulfilled the gratitude of his night.
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed dhikr for fulfilling daily gratitude in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a concise yet profound method for fulfilling the obligation of daily gratitude through the recitation of the final verse of Surah Al-Fatiha. This practice highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating specific dhikr routines into the daily rhythm of morning and evening, ensuring that the believer's spiritual state remains anchored in thankfulness throughout the cycle of day and night.
